articles.title: I tested 18 tools for removing cat hair. These are the 9 best to keep your home fur-free
articles.summary: I put a bevy of hair removal solutions to the test and found the best options for keeping your home fur-free. ‘Can’t imagine a cat not having this toy’: Your indoor cat is bored. Here’s how to fix it. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: When I first adopted my three cats Frankie, Joy and Olive, I was prepared for playtime, cuddles and upgrading my phone storage to have room for all of the photos I’d take of them. I was not as prepared for the sheer amount of fur three cats produced simply by existing. Since my cats have both light and dark hair, it’s not easy to hide their fur.

At times, it would be easier to leave my condo coated in a layer of cat fur at all times – but with the right tools, tidying up becomes much easier. It turns out, depending on the fabric makeup of your furniture and clothing, you’ll need a variety of tools to keep your home spotless. To find the very best hair removal tools, I looked into what was on the market and tried a variety of methods to see which ones worked the most efficiently. I also consulted a cleaning expert and cat behavioralist to find out just what works most purrfectly for our homes with furry friends.

articles.title: Dads and dudes: the two style clans that dominate menswear
articles.summary: The ‘dad’ look favours straight lines and muted colours, while ‘dudes’ prefer baggier clothes with adornments. There is a competition going on at the US Open this week and it’s not the one involving rackets and balls.
body: Tennis legend Roger Federer took to the court on Tuesday in navy blue polo shirt and shorts, navy blue sweatbands and navy blue socks. The cuts were trim and the top was tucked in. The young Spanish player Carlos Alcaraz wore a Nike vest, untucked and the colour of Ribena, maroon shorts, and trainers that looked like a sweetshop counter.

The players represent two style clans that are dominating current menswear: the dads and the dudes. If you’re not sure what side of the sartorial net they’re on, here’s a quick form guide. Novak Djokovic, Taylor Fritz and Félix Auger-Aliassime are all “dads”, while Arthur Fils and Andre Agassi are “dudes”.

Away from baselines and backhands, David Beckham in his slim, sometimes three-piece suits, actor Theo James, in real life as well as in Netflix series The Gentleman, the second series of which will land next week, Idris Elba and Andy Burnham are all prime examples of “dads”.
Dudes, meanwhile, include Brad Pitt, who appears on the cover of September’s Esquire in a red shirt with hot-pink neckerchief, Adam Sandler in chaotic ensembles, and men across Britain.
points: The ‘dad’ look favours straight lines and muted colours, while ‘dudes’ prefer baggier clothes with adornments.

articles.title: Infallible style: Pope Leo appears in Vanity Fair’s ranks of most fashionable
articles.summary: Pontiff, who has caught the eye in trainers and a baseball cap, praised for taking dress to ‘heavenly heights’ For the first time in a decade, Vanity Fair has released a best-dressed list. Featuring 70 names, the list ranks the most fashionable people in the world in 2026.
body: The 70-year-old head of the Catholic church has been praised by the magazine for taking papal style “to heavenly heights”. His most memorable look? A simple white cassock styled with a pair of Nike trainers.
Vanity Fair’s style correspondent José Criales-Unzueta, who worked on compiling the list, said he and the team were impressed by the “innate Americanness” of the way the pope dressed.

The Chicago-born pontiff has carved out a style niche and garnered a loyal fashion following with his enthusiasm for both bespoke vestments and vintage fashion accessories. Alongside trainers, he prefers simple black oxford shoes to the traditional red papal slippers.

He wears a discontinued Swiss-made quartz watch, carries his own battered briefcase and in June 2025 popped a White Sox baseball cap over his papal cap for a general audience in St Peter’s Square. For more formal occasions, he turns to the Italian designer Filippo Sorcinelli, who also created liturgical vestments for the previous popes Benedict XVI and Francis.

articles.title: ‘Still or Sparkling’ Must Be Stopped
articles.summary: All this week, the Eater Today newsletter is dedicated to editor Hot Takes, a way to release the pressure valve of crankiness that comes with sweating your way through the end of summer. This story was previously published as part of that series.
body: More and more often, my meal — even at ostensibly casual restaurants — begins not only with an attempted upsell, but with a question I’ve come to dread because of the weird stigma attached to my inevitable response.
You sit. Your server materializes. The question arrives: “Still or sparkling?” A beat. “Or filtered tap?”

It’s a strange way to begin an experience ostensibly centered on hospitality. Before I’ve had a chance to look at the menu, order a guava mezcal margarita, or even fully settle into my chair, I’m being asked whether I’d like to turn the most basic necessity on the table into a line item on the bill. Restaurants have plenty of opportunities to sell me things — that is, fundamentally, why I’m there — but surely the first sip of water can remain outside the machinery of the upsell.

articles.title: 8 Best Shampoos for Frizzy Hair, According to Hair Stylists and Vogue Editors
articles.summary: Can shampoo actually prevent hair frizz? Six pro hairstylists share everything you need to know; plus, shop Vogue’s edit of the best shampoos for frizzy hair.
body: After a trip to Puerto Vallarta this past June, I made a vow to myself: I will never again travel to a rainy, humid climate without a good shampoo for frizzy hair. Though the mountainous views were stunning, the state of my hair throughout my stay was not, and I spent my beach days in a tizzy of frizz.

Jackie Seabrooke, a celebrity hairstylist based in New York City, assured me that my hair nightmare was, alas, not unique. “When hair is dry and lacks moisture, it tries to absorb moisture from the air, causing the cuticle to swell and become frizzy,” she explained. “This is why hair tends to look even more frizzy in humid conditions.” But sometimes, unsightly frizz doesn’t even come with margaritas on the side.

Seabrooke said that even day-to-day activities—like washing with too-hot water, heat damage, rough towel drying, and genetics—can all play into hair that’s more staticky than silky. And though styling products can be a savior, frizz control starts in the shower.
points: Six pro hairstylists share everything you need to know; plus, shop Vogue’s edit of the best shampoos for frizzy hair.

articles.title: The Best NARS Products Have Serious Staying Power
articles.summary: The iconic ’90s beauty brand still holds up—in popularity and product wear time. From blush to foundation, these are the nine best NARS products according to Vogue.
body: For me, NARS is tied to some of my earliest memories of makeup. As a mid-’90s baby with a surprisingly sharp memory of my toddler years, I remember sneaking into my mom’s jade-green acrylic makeup case and pulling out products from the brand—including its iconic powder blushes with decidedly risqué names I was still too young to read.

While my own beauty bag options are much more varied, and my heavy-makeup phase as an alternative teenager may be behind me, there are still occasions that call for formulas capable of going the distance—say, the Met Gala. And while my relationship with makeup has changed considerably over the years, one thing has remained the same: blush is always a must.

articles.title: Garlic Confit
articles.summary: The sweet, jammy garlic cloves are only half the story—don’t sleep on the deeply savory oil.
body: Garlic confit transforms pungent raw cloves into a sweet, tender, jammy condiment by cooking them slowly in a bath of oil. A French technique classically used to preserve meat in its own rendered fat, confit can also be done, as it is here, with a neutral oil.

Most of the cooking time is hands-off. For an aromatic variation, add a few sprigs of rosemary or thyme, a bay leaf, black peppercorns, or crushed red pepper flakes before the pan goes into the oven (see Herby Garlic Confit ). And don’t overlook the oil. Garlic confit gives you two kitchen workhorses in one: Mash the cloves into potatoes or hummus, smear them onto toast, or mix them with softened butter for steak. Use the deeply savory garlic oil in salad dressings, marinades, or anywhere you want a mellow hit of garlic.

Most vegetable oils will work here. We prefer a neutral oil, such as grapeseed or safflower, which lets the garlic flavor shine. Extra-virgin olive oil is another good option, though its flavor can be overpowering here, and it tends to break down more quickly than a neutral variety. Avoid delicate oils, as well as canola, which develop off-flavors during the long cooking process.
points: The sweet, jammy garlic cloves are only half the story—don’t sleep on the deeply savory oil.
